disease_label_per_paper: Antibody-mediated rejection in a heart transplant recipient with cardiogenic shock requiring temporary mechanical circulatory support
presentation_summary: 57-year-old Black man presented 5 years after orthotopic heart transplantation with one week of dry cough, dyspnea, fatigue, abdominal pain, lower extremity edema, fever/chills history, and upper respiratory symptoms.

On presentation he had BP 84/62 mmHg, heart rate 111/min, respiratory rate 22/min, oxygen saturation 99% on 2 L, elevated JVP, bibasilar crackles, enlarged liver span, and bilateral lower extremity edema.

Workup showed creatinine 3.3 mg/dL from baseline 1.4, BNP 4900 pg/mL, bicarbonate 13, ECG sinus tachycardia with low voltage/right-axis deviation, chest radiograph pulmonary vascular congestion and mild cardiomegaly, LVEF <20%, cardiac index 1.6 L/min/m2, and PCWP 23 mmHg.
Endomyocardial biopsy pAMR/cellular rejection, pathology, DSA context, final diagnosis, treatment course, and recovery are preserved as confirmatory/non-ranking evidence.

quality_warnings: Biopsy pathology, pAMR grade, C4d, final diagnosis, treatment response, and outcome are non-ranking confirmatory/workup evidence.
The URI-like fever/chills and cough are preserved as rankable presentation evidence even though they are mimic-prone and cannot be hard-fixed away.
